name: Question 17
problem: Find matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=A,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix and $A=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 8 \\ -3 & 8\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.** We need to find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ using its characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-6-\lambda  & 8 \\ -3 & 8-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-6-\lambda )(8-\lambda )-(8)(-3) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -24 & =0 \\ (\lambda +4)(\lambda -6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $A$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=-4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=6.$

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$ 

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=-4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-4)I & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 8 \\ -3 & 8\end{aligned}]-(-4)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 \\ -3 & 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & 0 \\ -3 & 12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{3}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=4{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=6,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-6I & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 8 \\ -3 & 8\end{aligned}]-6[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 8 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 
So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 8 & 0 \\ -3 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{4}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-12 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ as follows:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
